task: Both lines print 12. Why do they look the same?

options.text: print() shows text without its quotes, so the number and the text look the same.
Python turns "12" into a number before printing it.
options.why: Python never changes a value's kind on its own. print() shows text without its quotes, so 12 and "12" print the same, but they are different kinds.
"12" is in quotes, so it is text (str), not a number.
Quotes change the kind. "12" is in quotes, so it is text (str), not a number.

ok: The first value is an int and the second is a str. print() shows both as 12.
